chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Similar to that, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is disliked out of fear that the ignorant one would button it. But as for the jurist, there is no problem if he wears it.'

key_terms.الْجَاهِلُ: The ignorant person, one lacking knowledge of ritual details
key_terms.الْفَقِيهُ: The jurist, one with deep knowledge of Islamic law
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/harm, indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَزُرَّهُ: He buttons it (specifically referring to fastening the garment)

ai.seo_question: Why is wearing buttoned clothing disliked for those in Ihram, and who is exempt from this dislike?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between the general public (al-jahil) and the learned scholar (al-faqih) regarding ritual prohibitions. It clarifies that the dislike (karahah) of wearing a buttoned cloak in Ihram is not an absolute invalidation but a precautionary measure to prevent the unlearned from committing errors, whereas the jurist’s awareness renders the act permissible.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> similar to that, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, that (wearing of a pillion) is disliked out of fear that the ignorant one would button it. But, as for the understanding one, so there is no problem if he were to wear it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
a similar Hadith and said that he called it undesirable because of fear that an ignorant person may button it, but in the case of a faqih it is not harmful. H 7178, Ch. 83, h 9
